tracks.title: AI Fluency & Verification
tracks.description: Use modern AI deliberately: frame work, provide context, verify claims, protect data, and keep human ownership.
tracks.outcome: A reusable AI workflow with a verification checklist and documented failure boundaries.
tracks.whyNow: AI use is becoming baseline; dependable judgment is the differentiator.

missions.title: Map capability and failure
missions.action: Test one task across two assistants and record where each succeeds, guesses, or refuses.
missions.proof: A comparison matrix with three verified failure modes.

missions.title: Engineer the context
missions.action: Turn a vague request into a goal, constraints, evidence, output contract, and stopping rule.
missions.proof: A reusable prompt template plus one before-and-after result.

missions.title: Build a verification gate
missions.action: Check sources, edge cases, security, and reproducibility before accepting an output.
missions.proof: A completed five-gate review.

missions.title: Make the final decision
missions.action: Write what the model contributed, what you rejected, and why the result is safe to use.
missions.proof: A short decision record with explicit human ownership.

tracks.title: Agentic Software Engineering
tracks.description: Design bounded agents that use tools, manage context, recover from failure, and pass measurable evaluations.
tracks.outcome: A small tool-using agent with an evaluation set, permissions boundary, and failure-handling plan.
tracks.whyNow: The durable skill is not calling a model; it is engineering a reliable loop around one.

missions.title: Choose the right boundary
missions.action: Separate deterministic code, model judgment, tool calls, and human approval.
missions.proof: A workflow diagram with stop and escalation conditions.

missions.title: Manage context deliberately
missions.action: Create compact instructions, task-specific memory, and a policy for what never enters context.
missions.proof: A context budget and data-handling checklist.

missions.title: Connect one safe tool
missions.action: Define a narrow tool contract, validate inputs, and make retries idempotent.
missions.proof: A tested tool schema with denied unsafe inputs.

missions.title: Evaluate the loop
missions.action: Build ten representative cases including failure, ambiguity, and adversarial input.
missions.proof: An eval report with pass rate and one improved failure.

tracks.title: Build & Ship AI Products
tracks.description: Move from a user problem to an evaluated AI feature with retrieval, observability, security, and cost controls.
tracks.outcome: A deployed thin-slice AI product whose quality and cost can be measured.
tracks.whyNow: Successful AI products need product judgment, evaluation, and operations—not only model access.

missions.title: Define the user decision
missions.action: Choose one narrow user problem and specify what a useful, harmful, and abstaining answer looks like.
missions.proof: A product brief with an initial evaluation set.

missions.title: Ground the response
missions.action: Add retrieval only where current or private source material is actually required.
missions.proof: A citation-aware prototype and retrieval failure cases.

missions.title: Measure quality and cost
missions.action: Track latency, cost, task success, unsupported claims, and user correction rate.
missions.proof: A small scorecard with thresholds.

missions.title: Ship the thin slice
missions.action: Deploy with access control, logging boundaries, fallback behavior, and a kill switch.
missions.proof: A live demo plus an operational readiness review.

references.label: Generative AI Learning Plan for Developers

tracks.title: Modern Full-Stack Delivery
tracks.description: Build a production-shaped web product with typed interfaces, tests, CI, containers, and observable releases.
tracks.outcome: A tested full-stack application with a deployment pipeline and documented operational decisions.
tracks.whyNow: Frameworks change; shipping a maintainable, testable product remains a durable engineering skill.

missions.title: Build one vertical slice
missions.action: Implement one user outcome across UI, API, validation, storage, and error states.
missions.proof: A working feature with typed boundaries.

missions.title: Test the risk
missions.action: Add unit, integration, and browser checks around the feature's highest-risk behavior.
missions.proof: A test plan connected to real failure modes.

missions.title: Automate delivery
missions.action: Create a pipeline that checks formatting, tests, security basics, and build output.
missions.proof: A green repeatable pipeline and a deliberately caught failure.

missions.title: Operate the release
missions.action: Add structured errors, health checks, rollback notes, and a lightweight cost estimate.
missions.proof: An operational runbook for the deployed feature.

tracks.title: Data, SQL & Applied ML
tracks.description: Turn messy data into a defensible decision using SQL, quality checks, baselines, models, and plain-language explanation.
tracks.outcome: A reproducible analysis or model with data-quality checks and a decision-focused explanation.
tracks.whyNow: AI increases the speed of analysis, but data quality and statistical judgment still determine whether it is useful.

missions.title: Start with the decision
missions.action: Write the decision, metric, grain, and minimum data required before opening a notebook.
missions.proof: A one-page analysis contract.

missions.title: Interrogate the data
missions.action: Check missingness, duplicates, leakage, time boundaries, and surprising distributions.
missions.proof: A data-quality report with one corrected defect.

missions.title: Beat a simple baseline
missions.action: Build the simplest credible query or model before adding complexity.
missions.proof: Baseline results and a justified improvement.

missions.title: Explain the decision
missions.action: State the result, uncertainty, limitation, and recommended next action without model jargon.
missions.proof: An executive summary plus reproducible code.

references.label: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL

tracks.title: Cloud, Serverless & FinOps
tracks.description: Design and operate a low-cost cloud workload with infrastructure as code, observability, security, and explicit cost limits.
tracks.outcome: A serverless service with an architecture diagram, budget guardrails, and operational runbook.
tracks.whyNow: Modern builders must understand both reliability and unit economics before scaling infrastructure.

missions.title: Choose the cheapest adequate shape
missions.action: Compare static, serverless, container, and managed options against traffic and reliability needs.
missions.proof: An architecture decision record with estimated cost drivers.

missions.title: Make infrastructure repeatable
missions.action: Describe resources, permissions, encryption, and deletion safety as code.
missions.proof: A reviewed change set with no public datastore.

missions.title: Observe the user outcome
missions.action: Define logs, metrics, alarms, and a trace from failure symptom to likely cause.
missions.proof: A dashboard or runbook with alert thresholds.

missions.title: Install cost guardrails
missions.action: Set a budget, identify variable-cost events, and create a frugal degradation plan.
missions.proof: A monthly cost envelope and shutdown checklist.

tracks.title: Secure AI & Software Delivery
tracks.description: Threat-model a product, protect identity and secrets, secure dependencies, and verify AI-specific abuse boundaries.
tracks.outcome: A security-reviewed application with a threat model, hardened authentication, and tested abuse cases.
tracks.whyNow: Fast AI-assisted delivery expands both capability and attack surface; secure defaults must move equally fast.

missions.title: Threat-model the outcome
missions.action: Map assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse paths, and the impact of failure.
missions.proof: A threat model with prioritized mitigations.

missions.title: Harden identity and data
missions.action: Verify authentication, authorization, session handling, storage exposure, and least privilege.
missions.proof: A security checklist with anonymous-access tests.

missions.title: Secure the delivery chain
missions.action: Review dependencies, build permissions, secret handling, and release provenance.
missions.proof: A dependency and pipeline risk report.

missions.title: Test AI abuse boundaries
missions.action: Probe prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool use, over-permission, and unsupported output.
missions.proof: An adversarial test set and one repaired control.

tracks.title: System Design, Debugging & Modern Interviews
tracks.description: Prepare for the complete engineering signal: coding, debugging, systems, project depth, behavioral impact, and responsible AI use.
tracks.outcome: A company-aware interview plan, two recorded simulations, and an evidence-backed project narrative.
tracks.whyNow: Hiring loops increasingly measure real engineering judgment beyond isolated algorithm recall.

missions.title: Diagnose the weakest signal
missions.action: Score coding, debugging, systems, project depth, behavior, and AI judgment honestly.
missions.proof: A prioritized two-week plan.

missions.title: Design and debug
missions.action: Design one service, then diagnose a realistic failure inside it.
missions.proof: An architecture plus hypothesis-driven incident review.

missions.title: Defend a real project
missions.action: Explain constraints, your contribution, alternatives, failure, and measured impact.
missions.proof: A ten-minute recorded deep-dive.

missions.title: Run the full simulation
missions.action: Combine a timed technical task with behavioral follow-up and self-review.
missions.proof: A rubric score and targeted repeat.

videos.title: Generative AI in a Nutshell
videos.creator: Henrik Kniberg
videos.why: Build a useful mental model before learning product-specific tricks.
videos.before: Write your current explanation of how a generative model produces an answer.
videos.after: Name two capabilities, two failure modes, and one decision that must remain human.

videos.title: But what is a neural network?
videos.creator: 3Blue1Brown
videos.why: Connect model behavior to a concrete visual representation instead of treating AI as magic.
videos.before: Sketch what you think a neuron and a layer represent.
videos.after: Explain weights, activations, and learning using one original example.

videos.title: Harvard CS50’s Artificial Intelligence with Python
videos.creator: freeCodeCamp.org
videos.why: Provides durable AI foundations behind current generative systems.
videos.before: Choose one section tied to your current project; do not watch the entire course passively.
videos.after: Implement one idea and record the test that demonstrates it works.

videos.title: Git and GitHub for Beginners
videos.creator: freeCodeCamp.org
videos.why: Version control remains the evidence trail behind modern human-and-AI software work.
videos.before: Predict what commit, branch, merge, and remote each control.
videos.after: Create a branch, make one focused commit, review its diff, and explain the history.

videos.title: Docker Tutorial for Beginners
videos.creator: TechWorld with Nana
videos.why: Containers remain a practical bridge between local development and repeatable deployment.
videos.before: Write the difference you expect between an image, container, volume, and network.
videos.after: Containerize one small service and explain its runtime boundary and secret-handling plan.
